title: "About"

## Background

I grew up in Dhaka, obsessed with science fiction and convinced I'd become a scientist who built robots and brain microchips that can copy paste skills. Life took a longer route. In grade 6 I started competitive debating, and the questions that stuck with me were the ones about economics: why do things work the way they do in an underdeveloped country, and who gets to decide. That pulled me toward studying economics, first at BRAC University, then a Master's at North South University, where my thesis used a causal-impact model employing Bayesian structural time series to estimate how COVID-19 affected Bangladesh's macroeconomy. The finding I could stand behind was a significant increase in foreign reserves. The rest of the results didn't survive their p-values, and I learned early how honest data work has to be with itself.

## From advertising to data science

Somewhere along the way I also fell in love with writing, so after graduation I spent seven years as a copywriter and creative manager at Asiatic MCL, the largest agency in Bangladesh. My clients included BRAC, Unilever, GSK, PepsiCo, Airtel, Toffee, USAID, and UKAID, among about fifty others. The work I'm proudest of came at the start of the pandemic: a joint project with BRAC and USAID where we built a rumour map of Bangladesh, tracking which misinformation was spreading in which districts, and then produced the TVCs, billboards, and targeted digital work to counter it. It was the first time I saw data and communication saving lives in the same breath.

## Why data science

The pivot started there and finished during my master's thesis, where R stopped being a tool and became a way of thinking. In advertising I built arguments from cultural insight. I want to build them from evidence I can defend line by line. I sat in enough boardrooms watching decisions turn on a chart no one felt qualified to question, and I got tired of being on the wrong side of that asymmetry. Data science is how I plan to close it, for myself and eventually for the teams and organisations I work with. UBC MDS is where I'm starting, because the program is built for people who care more about problems than about pedigree, and because learning in an environment tied to industry is how I know I learn best.

## Outside of data science

Weekends usually mean poker with friends, paddleboarding (something I picked up recently and can't get enough of), or a good film. I'll take a thriller, a crime story, sci-fi, or a slow drama, in any order. When none of that fits the mood, I disappear into a passion project and vibe-code my way through it until the sun is up. I play the guitar and love grunge, hip hop, and metal, though Murakami on the shelf and a FIFA session on the couch balance things out. I cook a killer khichuri and biryani, and if you've had my milk tea you already know. Right now I'm learning Japanese and French, studying chess seriously enough to lose sleep over it, and building the courage to try learning skydiving and scuba diving within the next year. I love writing poems and making short reels which are small love letters to the life I have and all the amazing people in it.
